To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy spectrum of the Crab nebula has been measured in the energy range from 1 TeV to 100 Tev with a statistical significance of 4.6σ.
the Milagro gamma ray observatory has made measurements of the TeV gamma ray energy spectra of the Crab nebula and other sources.

Milagro has observed a TeV spectrum for the Crab nebular which is consistent with atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, and has determined a TeV energy spectrum for the Cygnus region which is consistent with the spectrum determined by HESS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cosmic rays, gamma rays, neutrinos, and dark matter in the 10 TeV to 100 Tev range.
the study of the high energy gamma‐ray sky using the Milagro water Cherenkov detector.
the study of the energy spectrum of the gamma rays from the Crab nebula and the development of the energy reconstruction algorithm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Milagro is capable of determining source spectra with good statistics and reasonable accuracy.
the Milagro data are consistent with the hypothesis that the Crab Nebula is the source of the TeV gamma ray flux.
Milagro has the ability to make energy‐resolved measurements of the gamma ray flux from a source, and has the potential of being able to make spectral measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Milagro is a good atmospheric Cherenkov detector for sources with a spectral cutoff above ∼10 TeV, but is not sensitive for sources with a cutoff below ∼10 Te V.
the Milagro energy spectrum for the Crab nebular matches the spectrum measured by the atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes in the overlapping energy range.
we can determine the energy spectrum of sources in the 1‐100 TeV range with an accuracy of about a factor of two.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Milagro can determine spectra of sources with high precision.
Milagro can be used to estimate the energy spectrum of TeV gamma ray emitters.
the Milagro array can be used for spectral determination in the energy range from 1 to 10 TeV.
